transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Ever since my heart stopped, I go out of my way not to think or talk about what happened or anything to do with doctors. It has just become too difficult to face, and my wife finally convinced me that I need to talk to someone about how much I've been avoiding it all.
How long have you been experiencing these feelings of avoidance since the event occurred?
It’s been going on ever since that heart episode, which happened about two and a half years ago. It has been a constant struggle for me, and it really hasn't let up at all during this whole time.
Beyond avoiding thoughts and reminders of the event, have you also been experiencing symptoms like nightmares, flashbacks, or a persistent feeling of being on edge or easily startled?

Yes, I get these sudden flashbacks where I see myself back on the kitchen floor and hear my wife screaming, which is terrifying. I'm also constantly on edge, checking my pulse all the time and listening for any little noise. Because of that, my sleep is very light and jumpy, and I jerk awake at the slightest sound.
Since your heart episode two and a half years ago, have you experienced these symptoms continuously, or have there been periods where they went away for at least a month or more?

No, they haven't gone away at all. It has been completely continuous ever since it happened, and I haven't had even a month of relief. These feelings have been with me every single day for the last two and a half years.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports chronic, continuous symptoms of re-experiencing (flashbacks), avoidance, and hyperarousal lasting for 2.5 years without any period of remission. F43.11 (delayed onset) is excluded because symptoms began shortly after the event, and F43.12 (episodic) is excluded due to the continuous nature of the symptoms. Therefore, the diagnosis of chronic post-traumatic stress disorder is the most appropriate.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets the diagnostic criteria for Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) following a life-threatening medical event (cardiac arrest). He exhibits intrusive symptoms (flashbacks), persistent avoidance, and hyperarousal/hypervigilance, with symptoms lasting over two years and causing significant impairment.
